summaries.Good news: Communities are taking bold action on climate resilience and conservation: Boston is investing $10 billion in flood infrastructure, Indonesia's women divers are protecting coral reefs, and festivals are being redesigned to restore land rather than degrade it.
summaries.Ideas: The design and strategy world is grappling with hard truths: why good design fails inside companies despite solid research, how AI's real-world usage remains opaque, and why beige has conquered our homes while our relationship with technology grows more complicated.
summaries.Technology: From retro e-paper alarm clocks challenging our phone addiction to modular tiny homes and hiking gear that does more with less, practical innovation is quietly solving everyday friction points while AI safety becomes an urgent priority.
summaries.Design: Architecture and design are expanding their ambitions: OMA delivers San Francisco's first 100% affordable housing, heritage buildings like the Finsbury Health Centre are being reimagined for modern living, and designers are creating furniture that tells stories about justice and materiality.

items.title: OMA completes first US affordable housing development in San Francisco
items.snippet: The New York office of OMA and local practice YA Studio have arranged a 160-home apartment block in San Francisco, California, around multiple courtyards. Named 730 Stanyan, the development is OMA's first 100 per cent affordable housing complex in the United States. Set near Golden Gate Park and the
items.line: OMA's first fully affordable housing development demonstrates how design excellence and social mission can align at scale in one of America's most expensive housing markets.

items.snippet: Designer Shahar Livne has created The Devil's Milk, a collection of designs that investigate rubber production and its history of violence and abuse. The designs, which Livne created over two years, include a scale, a cabinet and a bench, made from different types of rubber. "The concept behind the
items.line: Shahar Livne's investigation of rubber production history through furniture design shows how material exploration can confront uncomfortable truths about colonialism and labor exploitation.

items.title: The extraordinary engineering that builds nature's only straight tusk
items.snippet: The narwhal's defining feature – its continuously growing tusk – is the only straight structure of its kind seen in nature. Now, scientists have cracked the code on how these elusive Arctic whales grow such an impressive and unique tool.Continue ReadingCategory: Biology, Science, Refractor: Science
items.line: Scientists cracking the engineering code of narwhal tusks—nature's only perfectly straight structure—could unlock principles for advanced materials design.

items.title: Why good design fails inside most companies
items.snippet: Most companies believe they understand their customers. They run research, track behavior, and gather feedback at scale. Yet products still reach the market feeling disconnected from the way people actually live. The original insight was there. It just became a little less clear each time it passed
items.line: An analysis of why good design fails inside companies despite solid research points to how insights get diluted as they move through organizational layers—a design system problem, not a research problem.
